title: Versioned price table
description: The rates that turn a token count into USD, with the window structure they depend on (KTD7). Versioned and committed rather than hardcoded for one reason: a rate change must not silently re-price history, so every ledger row records the identity of the table that produced its figure. Two things about this provider make the structure load-bearing rather than decorative. First, every rate is quoted at TWO prices, peak and off-peak, with off-peak exactly half; a table that carried one number would be wrong by a factor of two for part of every day. Second, the peak window is a wall-clock interval in UTC, so a cost is a function of WHEN a call happened, not only of what it consumed -- which means the timestamp used has to be recorded, and a call straddling a boundary has an ambiguity the provider does not document.

table_version.description: The table's own format version, read from this file by the loader rather than restated in Python.

source.description: Where the rates came from, as a URL. Required because a rate is a claim about the world: without a source it is an assertion, and this repo does not accept assertions about prices any more than about physics.

retrieved_at.description: ISO-8601 date the source was read. A rate without a retrieval date is unfalsifiable -- the page carries a standing notice that prices may change.

unit.description: Explicit rather than implied: `per_million_tokens` is how the provider quotes, and a consumer that assumed per-token would be off by six orders of magnitude.

peak_windows.description: The definition of the expensive window, transcribed. Off-peak is everything else, and is half the peak rate.

hours.description: Half-open intervals [start, end) in local hours, so the boundary belongs to exactly one window. The provider writes them as `01:00 - 04:00`, which does not say whether the endpoints are inclusive; half-open is the assumption this table makes, and the plan records it as an assumption rather than a fact, because getting it wrong doubles a bill or halves it.

models.description: Rates per API model name. Keyed by the name a request uses, and each entry records the model VERSION the provider maps it to -- which is how this file documents that `deepseek-flash` serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the version the plan originally mistook for an API name.

verification.description: Whether the rates have been checked against the provider's own accounting, and how. `unverified` means the numbers are transcribed from documentation -- which is an inherited figure, not a measurement, and must not be described as measured. The `method` field names how any verification was done (a balance delta), and `observations` carries what was seen so a reader can judge the tolerance rather than trust it.

rate_set.description: The three rates a call's cost is computed from. Input is split by cache status because the provider prices a cache hit at roughly a fiftieth of a miss, and output is one rate -- reasoning tokens are billed as output, which is why the ledger's usage record treats `reasoning_tokens` as a SUBSET of `completion_tokens` rather than a separate line.
